events.title: Ruairidh kneels first to Cupa na Fìrinne
events.body: At Seann Skell, Ruairidh, a sworn-man of the harbour-court, crosses the quay stones and kneels before his own son Mànas mac Ruairidh, the first of the preaching's hearers to do so. Six other net-menders kneel after him before the tide has gone out much further.

events.title: Tidings of the king's death reach the quay
events.body: A rider watering his horse at Seann Skell's harbour-court brings word that Lachlann mac Iain has died at Cathair dhearg, eighty-nine years old after a reign of fifty quiet years, and that his daughter Anna, fifty-four, has been crowned in his place. Mànas mac Ruairidh is not recorded to have said anything of it.

events.title: The first boats blessed at Cidhe an Diosail
events.body: A dozen coasters are brought up one after another to Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell, and Mànas mac Ruairidh passes a plain wooden bowl of harbour water over each hull in turn, speaking the words that harden, within his own lifetime, into the fixed form of the rite of blessing.

events.title: The harbour-court's scribe refuses the order's rite
events.body: Donnchadh mac Ailein, scribe of the harbour-court at Seann Skell, refuses to enter the blessings of Òrd Mhanannain in Rolla a' Chalaidh beside the tallies of hulls and cargoes, holding a rite to be no business of a board kept for hulls. Mànas does not press the matter.

events.title: Tormod Ciar swears Cupa na Fìrinne on the rope-walk
events.body: At Cuan shean, the old rope-walker Tormod Ciar, told by a travelling net-mender what Mànas mac Ruairidh preaches of the mist, swears Cupa na Fìrinne before his fellow walkers on the rope-walk itself, cupping rainwater in his own hands for want of a bowl, with no priest of the order present to hear him.

events.title: Taigh Mhanannain raised at Seann Skell
events.body: Òrd Mhanannain raises its own house at Seann Skell, Taigh Mhanannain, low and built of the same grey stone as the quay near the old harbour-court. The congregation raises the silver for a proper cup without being asked, to replace the plain wooden bowl Mànas has used since the first blessing.

events.title: Birth of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona
events.body: A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna's heir, then five-and-forty years old, in the six-and-twentieth year of Queen Anna's reign; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year and not the name.

events.title: Death of Queen Anna
events.body: Queen Anna dies at Cathair dhearg at five-and-eighty, one-and-thirty years crowned, the last of the house of Catrìona whose name Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps for more than a century.

events.title: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona crowned
events.body: Anna's heir is crowned at Cathair dhearg within the season, fifty years old. Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the reign's years and not its name.

events.title: Death of Mànas mac Ruairidh
events.body: Mànas mac Ruairidh dies at Seann Skell in the house he raised, six-and-thirty years after his first preaching on the quay, and is buried at his own asking under a plain slab facing the harbour mouth. Beathag nic Dhonnchaidh, who kept his house, keeps Taigh Mhanannain after him.

events.title: The rule of the headlands laid down
events.body: After a winter's debate, the priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag lay down that no boat of the faithful may sail out of sight of the headlands, on pain of answering for it before Cupa na Fìrinne. The rule holds on the west coast far beyond any one preacher's lifetime.

events.title: Coinneach mac Sheumais turned back within the year
events.body: Coinneach mac Sheumais, a skipper of Ros bheag, is turned back within the rule's first year by two of the order's own boats after taking his own boat further out than before, chasing a good run of fish. He never fishes so far out again.

events.title: Griogair cannot name his grandfather's star
events.body: A priest of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag asks a boy named Griogair, grandson of one of the last pilots to hold a course by night on that shore, which star his grandfather steered by. The boy cannot answer, and no one in his own house had thought to write the star's name down.

events.title: The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt
events.body: The royal granaries at Àth shean, standing since before a' Scaradh, are pulled down and rebuilt in dressed stone on raised floors against the rats, along with a new tally-house. Fearchar mac Phàdraig, the reeve who oversees the three-year labour, sees the shire's grain stand dry through its first winter.

events.title: Murchadh Beag takes Eòghann mac Pheadair from the coal-face
events.body: The old scribe of Taigh na Fèithe, Murchadh Beag, hears a coal-breaker's young son recite back a whole day's cartage without once looking at the board, and asks the boy's father whether a household might spare him for a scribe's stool. Eòghann mac Pheadair is set to sweep Taigh na Fèithe floor and mix ink before he is let touch a leaf.

events.title: Taigh na Fèithe's leaf takes in the rope-ground sown with barley
events.body: Eòghann mac Pheadair, fourteen and newly trusted with a leaf of his own, enters the ground given up by Cuan shean's rope-walks for barley, the first entry he copies whose full sense Murchadh Beag has to explain to him. He learns that a scribe's business is the fact and the year, not the grief behind it.

events.title: Death of the fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona
events.body: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at seven-and-eighty after seven-and-thirty years crowned, and the heir, two-and-forty years old, is crowned the same season.

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair at four-and-twenty
events.body: At four-and-twenty Eòghann mac Pheadair has old Murchadh Beag's stool at Taigh na Fèithe as good as his own, and enters the wave at Cnoc chaol on the general leaf as he enters every disaster that touches a household of the coal-right: names, place, day.

events.title: A household of Cnoc chaol removes its gallery-claim from the shore
events.body: After the great wave that took two children from the beach at Cnoc chaol, the household of one of the drowned strikes itself from its old gallery and takes up a new claim further from the water. Eòghann mac Pheadair enters the removal on Taigh na Fèithe's leaf the following season, cold and plain as he was taught.

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair witnesses the market bounds at Baile Mòr dhìreach
events.body: Sent east on his own feet for the first time, Eòghann mac Pheadair stands witness for Na Seachd Taighean when the crown's grant of a market is read at Baile Mòr dhìreach and its boundary stones set. He watches the first stalls go up the same afternoon and walks the road home slower than he walked out.

events.title: Mòrag nic Ìomhair rides to Taigh na Fèithe with the crown's leaves
events.body: A scribe of An Talla Dearg's own household, Mòrag nic Ìomhair, rides the thirty-nine miles to Taigh na Fèithe at Muileann dhearg to set the crown's reckoning of Bliadhnaichean an Diosail against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own, after the two offices' counts are found not to agree. The master of Taigh na Fèithe grants her the book for as many days as the matter takes.

events.title: The fault in the count is found and cannot be mended
events.body: Working three days by lamplight, Eòghann mac Pheadair and Mòrag nic Ìomhair trace the two offices' counts of An Diosal back to a single year, early after An Diosal, entered twice by one office's habit or once by the other's. Neither leaf either scribe has brought can say which office erred, or whether either truly has.

events.title: The two counts settled by agreement, not by proof
events.body: Taigh na Fèithe and the crown's scribe take the crown's count for the reckoning that will go forward, since it touches more households than Taigh na Fèithe's own, and Eòghann mac Pheadair writes Taigh na Fèithe's agreement to it in his own hand. The master of Taigh na Fèithe's mark is set under his, and the crown scribe's office mark under that.

events.title: The day of Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh fixed
events.body: The same agreement that settles the count also fixes, for the first time, a single day on which Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh is to be kept by every harbour of the coast together, in place of each keeping it a day or two either side of its neighbours by its own old custom. Mòrag nic Ìomhair carries word of it down to Seann Skell.

events.title: The agreement-leaf folded into Leabhar a' Chùraim
events.body: Eòghann mac Pheadair keeps his copy of the sealed agreement between two older leaves of Leabhar a' Chùraim that had never before had a stranger's mark folded in among them. He tells the master of Taigh na Fèithe only that the crown's scribe was a hard woman to argue a figure past and an easy one to agree a figure with.

events.title: The coast keeps the rite on the agreed day
events.body: Mòrag nic Ìomhair writes to Eòghann mac Pheadair the following winter that not a single harbour of the coast has written to complain of the day set for Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh. Eòghann keeps the short note folded inside his own working leaves for the rest of his working life.

events.title: Birth of Eilidh Bhàn
events.body: A girl, Eilidh, fair enough to be called Eilidh Bhàn from her first year, is born at Cathair dhearg, granddaughter of the ruler who has then held the hall nine-and-twenty years.

events.title: Word of the disputation at Inis mhòr reaches Taigh na Fèithe
events.body: A rider carries north country talk to Taigh na Fèithe of a house of disputation newly founded at Inis mhòr, whose first master refuses every answer offered him on whether the vein answers any true count of years or only the custom of counting it. Eòghann mac Pheadair, old now, hears it out and goes back to his leaf.

events.title: The master of Taigh na Fèithe stands for Eòghann at the crowning
events.body: When Na Seachd Taighean' custodians go down to Cathair dhearg to see the new queen crowned, as the compact requires, the master of Taigh na Fèithe goes in place of Eòghann mac Pheadair, whose legs will no longer answer for a journey of thirty-nine miles in a single season. Eòghann hears the crowning described to him afterward by the returning master.

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair is carried to the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: In the last cold turn of the year, his chest gone tight in a way no winter before has managed, Eòghann mac Pheadair lets himself be carried by cart to the rebuilt bath-house below Muileann ruadh, where he sits in the warm water among coal-breakers, salt-carriers and a shepherd's widow, none of them minding whose gallery the others answer to.

events.title: Eòghann mac Pheadair shows the agreement-leaf to his own pupil
events.body: Asked by the young scribe he has lately taken to teaching what the finest thing was that he ever did in a life spent mostly at a stool, Eòghann mac Pheadair unfolds the thirty-year-old agreement-leaf and tells the boy it was not the count that made it worth keeping, but the honest agreement written under it.

events.title: Death of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona
events.body: The fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at nine-and-eighty after seven-and-forty years crowned, and the crown passes to a granddaughter, Eilidh Bhàn, eighteen years old.

events.title: A coaster boarded off the small islands
events.body: A coaster out of Ros bheag puts in at Baile chrom two days late and a third short in her hold, her skipper telling Coinneach mac Nèill, the reeve, that three boats out of the small islands boarded her and took her grain, wearing no mark and hiding no face.

events.title: Rolla a' Chalaidh name Aonghas mac Ruairidh among the sea-thieves
events.body: The first full count of the takings sent up to Cathair dhearg names, among the sea-thieves of the small islands, a fisherman's son of Baile chrom, Aonghas mac Ruairidh. His mother tells the reeve plainly that a young man who watches the fish thin will go looking for a living wherever it is still to be found.

events.title: Half of Baile chrom stands empty
events.body: Coinneach mac Nèill reports to the crown's scribes that half the houses of Baile chrom stand empty, their families gone inland before the sea-thieves and the failing catch, their thatch going to moss and their doors shut on rooms no one will sleep in again that year.

events.title: Baile chrom's grain dues remitted
events.body: The crown remits Baile chrom's grain dues to a sum reckoned by the households that stand rather than the households that once stood, answering Coinneach mac Nèill's plain report with a plain word of thanks for a count taken with care.

events.title: Birth of Dòmhnall Ruadh
events.body: A son, red-haired and called Dòmhnall Ruadh, is born at Muileann chrom to a custodian household of Clann Raghnaill that keeps three galleries under the mountain and has never once been asked into An Talla Dearg except to petition.

events.title: The reeve's letter asking for a force
events.body: After the sea-thieves put in twice within a single moon on strands within sight of his own harbour, Coinneach mac Nèill writes to the crown asking not for lightened dues this time but for an armed force, since a reeve with a tally-stick can no longer hold a coast his own shire's desperate sons have made their hunting ground.

events.title: Iain mac Thormoid raised against the small islands
events.body: Eilidh Bhàn raises a force under a captain named Iain mac Thormoid and sends it north by sea to Baile chrom, answering the reeve's long-waited letter. The captain charts the raiders' ground on Coinneach mac Nèill's own table with the help of the town's fishermen before the boats sail against the small islands.

events.title: Creach Eilean dhubh
events.body: Iain mac Thormoid's boats land at first light on Eilean dhubh and burn the sea-thieves' hulls on the strand, Coinneach mac Nèill's own fishermen leading the way through the channel among the small islands. The sea-thieves, unwatched for the better part of a decade, are taken all but by surprise.

events.title: Aonghas mac Ruairidh dies on the strand
events.body: Aonghas mac Ruairidh, thirty-one years old and once a boy Coinneach mac Nèill carried on his own shoulder to this same water, is killed defending a hull on Eilean dhubh's strand. The reeve kneels over him and finds he has no words ready for the mother he must tell of it.

events.title: Uilleam Ruadh taken and hanged
events.body: Uilleam Ruadh, leader of the sea-thieves for the better part of a decade, is taken alive off Eilean dhubh's strand and carried south in irons to Cathair dhearg, where he is hanged before the season turns, six and thirty years old.

events.title: The dearth on the north-west shore
events.body: A run of failed harvests along the north-west shore grows more than the shared-meal custom can carry. Coinneach mac Nèill keeps the custom at his own board as long as grain remains to keep it with, dividing what the diminished fields bring in as evenly as his hand can manage.

events.title: Beathag nic Artair dies of the winter's sickness
events.body: In the hard winter of the dearth, Beathag nic Artair, wife of the reeve of Baile chrom, dies of a chest complaint her body, weakened by two thin harvests running, has no strength left to fight. The last of the town's households load their carts and go inland and east the same season.

events.title: Coinneach mac Nèill leaves Baile chrom
events.body: Coinneach mac Nèill, reeve of Baile chrom for eight-and-forty years, sets the reeve's chest of rolls and tallies in order for a successor he no longer believes will come, shuts his own door behind him, and sets the coast road east under his feet.

events.title: Birth of Raghnall Òg
events.body: A son, Raghnall, is born at Muileann chrom to Dòmhnall Ruadh, then five-and-thirty years old and keeper of his house's three galleries.

events.title: Clàr nan Rìghrean recopied
events.body: The queen's scribes at Cathair dhearg take down the old Clàr nan Rìghrean from its resting place and copy it afresh onto new hide, adding every ruler since the fleet had gone and setting the new copy's beginning at An Roghnachadh rather than at the sailing.

events.title: The strand-market at Àth fhionn
events.body: A market grows up on the strand at Àth fhionn, where the coast road crosses the clear river, trading north-coast fish, the flesh and oil of stranded whales, wool and barley. The fishers of the north coast no longer carry their catch the longer road south to Inis mhòr.
